units: <cite ref="Sotah 10b:3">Sot. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>דבר זה מ׳ בידינו מאבותינו וכ׳</he> we hold a tradition from our fathers that &c.

Ḥull. 63ᵇ עוף טהור נאכל במ׳ as for eating clean birds we rely on tradition (there being no rules for distinguishing them in the Biblical law).—Esp. the traditional Scriptural text without vowels, contrad. to מקרא the traditional vocalization, v. אֵם.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Megillah 4:1:9">Y. Meg. IV, 74ᵈ</cite> bot. (ref. to <cite ref="Nehemiah 8:8">Neh. VIII, 8</cite>) ‘they explained the reading’, <he>זה המ׳</he> this means the traditional text; Bab.
<cite ref="Megillah 3a:8">Meg. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>אלו המסורות</he> (some eds. <cite ref="M01884"><he>מסורת</he></cite>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.); <cite ref="Nedarim 37b:5">Ned. 37ᵇ</cite> <he>המסורות</he>.
<cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:13">Ab. III, 13</cite> <he>מ׳ סייג לתורה</he> the tradition is the fence for (preserving the integrity of) the Torah.

<cite ref="Zevachim 37b:16">Zeb. 37ᵇ</cite>, sq. <he>אהני מקרא ואהני מ׳</he> the traditional vocalization is a help (in interpretation), and so is the traditional literal text (e. g. <he>בסכת</he>, <cite ref="Leviticus 23:42">Lev. XXIII, 42</cite>, which may be interpreted as singular number, and which is read as a plural); a. fr.—Pl. <he>מַסּוֹרוֹת</he>. Tanḥ. Vaëthḥ. 6 <he>נטלו מ׳ חכמה וכ׳</he> the traditions of wisdom were taken from Moses and given to Joshua.—
Meg. 3ᵃ; Ned. 37ᵇ, v. supra.—[מַסּוֹרָה Massorah, the collection of textual readings systematically arranged.]
